_note: The DSX Scene TRANSFORM corpus (dsx-scene.md P1). THE LAW: matrices are COLUMN-MAJOR mat4 (index = column*4 + row), vectors are columns (v' = M·v). A node's LOCAL matrix composes scale, then rotation, then translation — local = T · Rz(rz) · Ry(ry) · Rx(rx) · S — i.e. the X rotation applies to the object first, then Y, then Z (degrees, the authored `rotation="rx ry rz"` triple). WORLD = parentWorld · local, root downward. Vectors are space-separated triples; a malformed triple falls back to THAT attribute's default with exactly one diagnostic (Article 7 — never a crash, never a partial parse of the triple). JSE holes ({{ expr }}) interpolate before parsing: each case's `vars` map is the resolver — the runner substitutes String(vars[expr]) for every hole, exactly what the reactive store does live. Case shape: `tree` = a scene-node subtree (kind/id/position/rotation/scale/children as AUTHORED STRINGS); `node` = the id whose world matrix is asserted; `world` = the 16 column-major floats (6 decimals); `point` = optional {local, world} transformed point through that matrix; `diagnostics` = expected diagnostic count (absent = 0). Expected numbers were computed by an independent scratch implementation, never by the kernel under test. Runners: TS (packages/kernel/test/scene-conformance.test.ts, per-PR). Kotlin (:core) and Swift (record lane) are the P2 row of dsx-scene.md.
